items_missed: Customer asked 'how are you?' and Chris answered but never asked back
No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' confirmation
Never asked about stairs or floors at the destination (11532 Lafitte Lane) — origin is a ground-level storage unit, but the delivery address was never characterized at all
No special-considerations probe — no long walks, narrow hallways, or tight turns at either end
No access-concern probe — no parking, gate access, or unit-location questions at the storage facility or the house
No Worries Damage Coverage never mentioned — notable on a call that opened with him crediting the customer $210 for fifteen blankets left behind on the last move
On-Time Guarantee never mentioned even while setting the 8:30-9:00 AM window
No 'does that make sense?' sense-check after a dense pricing and clock block
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech skipped — staging items near the roll-up door and taking a carload still apply on a storage-unit origin
Walk distance never discussed, which matters at a storage facility where truck-to-unit distance drives the clock
Customer asked 'what do we do to secure the date?' — the textbook opening for 'no deposit required' — and it was never said
No bolded-details list or 'reply with any corrections' when describing the move confirmation email
No 'any other questions before I let you go?'
Never used the customer's name once — and the customer had to ask 'your name is Chris, right?' at the end
top_strength: Textbook proactive honesty. He surfaced the $210 blanket credit the customer hadn't even called about, then flagged the $150 North branch transportation fee before the customer could be surprised by it, broke it down as $75 out and $75 back, and offered Tuesday or Thursday as ways to avoid it entirely. The estimate reasoning was also strong — he anchored on the prior move's 6.75 hours and revised down to about 6 to 6.25 because everything is still wrapped.
coaching_note: The pricing mechanics were his best of the week, but he never characterized the destination — no floors, no stairs, no parking, no walk distance for 11532 Lafitte Lane — which is exactly the kind of gap that blows an estimate past the 20% accuracy band. Lock in destination access on every booking, and say 'no deposit required' out loud the moment a customer asks how to secure the date.
phone_presence_notes: Genuinely warm and personable — 'love hearing that' when the customer praised Shay and Thomas, then promised to pass the compliment along, and closed with 'it's a pleasure getting to work with you again' — held back from a 5 only by never once using the customer's name.
